sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Loads settings and the database client
sections.what: Loads the environment settings from the project folder, then imports the shared Supabase client.
sections.why: The settings must exist before the client can connect.
sections.watch_out: Import statements can run before the settings load, and the code does not make the order clear.

sections.name: defaultHackathons (part 1)
sections.title: Fixed hackathon sample records
sections.what: Holds the first set of sample hackathon records, including names, dates, team roster, tech stack and status.
sections.why: Gives the database a known starting set of hackathon entries.
sections.watch_out: These records include personal details, so anyone with the source can read them.

sections.name: defaultHackathons (part 2)
sections.title: Rest of the hackathon sample records
sections.what: Finishes the hackathon list with the last sample entries and closes it.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Any edit to these records changes what the migration writes.

sections.name: defaultInternships
sections.title: Fixed internship sample records
sections.what: Holds the sample internship records with company, role, status, location, salary, applied date and notes.
sections.why: Gives the database a known starting set of internship entries.
sections.watch_out: Some entries have no deadline date, so views that need one may show a gap.

sections.name: migrateData
sections.title: Writes records and counts them
sections.what: Finds one profile ID or falls back to a fixed ID. Attaches that ID to every record and saves both lists with upsert. Prints the result for each table and then the row counts.
sections.why: Puts sample data under one owner in a single run.
sections.watch_out: The fallback ID belongs to no real user, so records saved with it may be hidden or fail a foreign key check.

summary: Writes a fixed set of sample hackathon and internship records into the Supabase database and then counts them.
purpose: Loads the app's sample starting data into the database in one step.
why: Reason not stated in the code. Likely reason: to move the locally stored sample data into the database.
how: Load environment settings and the Supabase client. Hold the two fixed record lists. Look up one profile ID, or use a fixed fallback ID. Attach that ID to each record, save both lists with upsert, and count the rows in each table.
inputs: The Supabase settings, the fixed sample records in the file, and the profiles table.
outputs: Success or error messages and row counts in the terminal, plus new or updated rows in the database.
risks: The fallback ID matches no real user. The first profile found is used, which may not be the owner. Personal details are stored in the source file. Upsert overwrites rows with the same ID on each run.
debug: If rows appear under the wrong user, check the profile lookup. If saving fails, read the error message and check the table columns. If counts are low, check the access rules.
